batchName: Empire: From Constantine's Sons to Theodosius (AD 337-395) - Easy Batch 2
chapterName: Empire: From Constantine's Sons to Theodosius (AD 337-395)

questions.question: What was Julian's first act after entering Constantinople as sole emperor?
options: Leading the Christian funeral of Constantius
questions.explanation: Julian led his cousin's Christian funeral to show publicly that he was the lawful successor. Some sources say Constantius had named him heir on his deathbed.
questions.sourceQuote: His first act was to lead the Christian funeral of his cousin, a public show that he was the lawful successor.

questions.question: Which son did ancient writers blame for the purge of the imperial family in 337?
questions.explanation: Ancient writers blamed the middle son, Constantius II, for the killings. He went on to outlive both of his brothers.
questions.sourceQuote: Soldiers murdered most of the old emperor's other male relatives, a purge that ancient writers blamed on the middle son, Constantius II, the brother who would outlast them all.

questions.question: What nickname did Christians give Julian?
questions.explanation: Christians remembered Julian as "the Apostate" for abandoning their faith. He was the last non-Christian to rule the Roman Empire.
questions.sourceQuote: Julian, remembered by Christians as "the Apostate", was the last non-Christian to rule the Roman Empire.

questions.question: Which famous last words does legend attribute to the dying Julian?
questions.explanation: Legend gives his last words as "You have won, Galilean" (Vicisti, Galilaee). The phrase is considered an invention.
questions.sourceQuote: Legend says his last words were "You have won, Galilean" (*Vicisti, Galilaee*), "the Galilean" being his scornful name for Jesus, but this is considered invented.

questions.question: Which bishop refused Theodosius communion after the massacre at Thessalonica?
questions.explanation: Ambrose, the forceful bishop of Milan, demanded that the emperor do penance first. Theodosius agreed and attended church without his imperial robes until Christmas.
questions.sourceQuote: Ambrose, the forceful bishop of Milan, wrote to the emperor refusing him communion until he did penance.

questions.question: After abandoning Christianity, which god did Julian say he had followed for twelve years?
questions.explanation: Julian wrote that he spent twenty years as a Christian and twelve following Helios, the sun god. He quietly abandoned Christianity at around the age of 20.
questions.sourceQuote: He later wrote that he had spent twenty years as a Christian and twelve following Helios, the sun god.

questions.question: Which mystical philosophy, built on the ideas of Plato, did the young Julian study?
questions.explanation: Julian studied Neoplatonism, a mystical philosophy based on Plato's ideas. He even sought out a mentor who practised theurgy, magical rituals meant to call down the gods.
questions.sourceQuote: He studied Neoplatonism, a mystical philosophy built on the ideas of Plato.

questions.question: What did Julian's School Edict forbid Christians to do?
questions.explanation: The School Edict stopped Christians from teaching classical literature. It sneered that if they wanted literature, they had Luke and Mark.
questions.sourceQuote: His School Edict stopped Christians from teaching the classics: "If they want to learn literature, they have Luke and Mark," it said.

questions.question: Where in Thessalonica did Roman soldiers kill thousands of civilians in 390?
questions.explanation: Soldiers took revenge for the murder of a general by slaughtering civilians in the city's racetrack. Theodosius was far away in Milan at the time.
questions.sourceQuote: Roman soldiers then took revenge in the city's racetrack, killing thousands of civilians.

questions.question: What happened to the empire after Theodosius died in 395?
options: The Goths took control of the western half
The Senate chose a single new emperor
A Frankish general seized the whole of it
His sons split it into eastern and western courts
questions.explanation: His two young sons divided the empire into eastern and western courts. That division lasted until the west fell in the late 5th century.
questions.sourceQuote: His two young sons, Arcadius and Honorius, split the empire into eastern and western courts, a division that lasted until the west fell in the late 5th century.
